s: In respect of environmental protection, which of the following statements is true?
o: at the present level of development, environmental protection is not a luxury
environmental protection is an expensive proposition
It is difficult to assess the damages due to violation of ecological and environmental limits
economic growth will necessarily suffer in the short-run if environment protection measures are implemented

s: Which one of the following is not related to environmental protection ?
x: Poverty alleviation is not related to environmental protection. Major current environmental issues may include climate change, pollution, environmental degradation, and resource depletion. Poverty alleviation refers to efforts and strategies aimed at reducing or eliminating poverty, improving the wellbeing of individuals and communities, and providing access to the resources needed for a dignified life. It encompasses a variety of actions, from government policies to grassroots programs, that address both the symptoms and root causes of poverty. Sustainable Development Goals *The United Nations has identified 17 Sustainable Development Goals which have to be realised by the year 2030. These goals are - (1) No Poverty : End poverty in all its forms everywhere. (2) Zero Hunger : End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture. (3) Good Health and Well Being: Ensure healthy lives & promote well-being for all at all ages. (4) Quality Education: Ensure inclusive and equitable education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all. (5) Gender Equality: Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls. (6) Clean Water and Sanitation: Ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all. (7) Affordable and Clean Energy: Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all. (8) Decent Work and Economic Growth: Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full a

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three classic pillars of sustainable development?
x: The three classic pillars are economic development, social equity and environmental protection. Military security is not one of them.

s: In business terms, what does the triple bottom line of sustainable development stand for?
x: The triple bottom line is commonly expressed as People, Planet and Profit, corresponding broadly to social, environmental and economic concerns.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: According to the principle "Polluter shall pay", who should bear the cost of cleaning up pollution?
o: The person or company responsible for causing pollution

s: The "Polluter Pays" principle seeks to
o: Collect pollution tax from all industries
Create a compensation fund by the Government as it is the biggest polluter
Recover financial cost of preventing or remedying environmental damage from the polluter

s: What does the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) imply?
o: Responsibilities are shared, but developed nations carry greater duties
Only developing countries bear responsibility for environmental protection
All countries have identical environmental duties and identical capacities
Environmental duties are restricted to countries that caused no historical pollution
x: CBDR recognises shared responsibility while assigning greater duties to developed nations in view of their capacities and historical contribution.

s: The National Green Tribunal is required to apply which combination of principles while adjudicating environmental cases?
o: Sustainable development, precautionary principle and polluter-pays principle
Public trust doctrine, absolute liability and eminent domain
Common but differentiated responsibilities, prior appropriation and res judicata
Inter-generational equity, federal supremacy and parliamentary privilege
x: The NGT must apply the principles of sustainable development, precautionary action and polluter pays.

s: Which principle says that lack of full scientific certainty is no reason to postpone cost-effective measures against environmental harm?
x: This is the precautionary principle; it does not allow preventive action to be postponed until full certainty.

s: Which of the following runs counter to sustainable development?
o: Maximising economic growth at any cost
x: Maximising growth at any cost conflicts with sustainable development, which balances economic, social and environmental concerns.

s: What does the principle of carrying capacity in sustainable development mean?
o: The polluter bears the cost of pollution control
Human use must stay within what ecosystems can support
x: Carrying capacity means using resources within what ecosystems can support; the other options describe CBDR, polluter pays and precaution.

s: Which principle of sustainable development holds that the present generation must not deplete resources at the cost of future generations?
x: Intergenerational equity is the heart of the Brundtland definition: today's users hold resources in trust for future users.

s: Which principle of sustainable development makes the polluter bear the cost of preventing and controlling pollution?
x: Under the polluter pays principle, the cost falls on the polluter, not on the public.

s: Sustainable development exactly means:
o: Improving the conditions of present generation without affecting the needs of future generation
Development that percolates to the bottom level sections in the society
Development that lasts for a long time
x: Improving the conditions of present generation without affecting the needs of future generation Sustainable development, as defined by the Brundtland Commission, means development that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.It balances economic growth with environ mental and social considerations. This concept underlies most modern development policy frameworks.

s:
This question consist of two statements –
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R). Answer the question selecting the appropriate option given below:
Assertion: Economic sustainability primarily involves maximizing profits without considering social or environmental impacts.
Reason: Economic sustainability seeks to achieve a balance between economic growth, social equity.
o: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
Both the assertion and reason are true, but the reason is NOT a correct explanation of the assertion.
The assertion is true, but the reason is false.
The reason is true, but the assertion is false.
x: The assertion is false, since economic sustainability does not mean maximising profits while ignoring social and environmental factors. The reason is true because SD balances economic, social and environmental concerns.

s: A country’s natural capital included all of the following except:
x: ‘Natural capital includes all renewable and non-renewable environmental resources. It includes air, water, land, minerals and forests. In other words only those resources, which are created by nature, without any human interference, can be deemed as natural capital. Hence, roads cannot be included in the country’s natural capital.

s: A country’s natural capital includes all of the following except
x: Natural capital is made up of resources created by nature such as air, water, land, minerals and forests. Roads are man-made, so they are not natural capital.

s: Which of the following is consistent with the scope of sustainable development?
o: Running down natural capital to maximise current output
Excluding disadvantaged groups from development planning
Treating environmental protection and development as mutually exclusive
Meeting present needs while promoting equity within and across generations
x: Sustainable development includes meeting present needs, equity within and across generations, and inclusion. It rejects depletion of natural capital and the opposition of environment to development.

s: How does the National Environment Policy, 2006 treat conservation and livelihood security?
o: Objectives relevant only to urban areas
x: The National Environment Policy, 2006 holds that conservation and livelihood security are linked rather than opposed.

s: The Wetlands (Conservation & Management) Rules, 2010 were framed on the recommendation of an Expert Panel under which policy?
o: National Action Plan on Climate Change, 2008
x: An Expert Panel constituted under the National Environment Policy, 2006 led to the Wetlands Rules, 2010.

s: Which of the following is excluded from the scope of sustainable development?
o: Growth that runs down natural capital
x: Sustainable development includes present needs, equity and inclusion, but excludes growth that runs down natural capital.

s:
Assertion (A): Economic sustainability does not mean maximising profits without considering social or environmental impacts.
Reason (R): Sustainable development seeks a balance between economic growth, social equity and environmental protection.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Both are true, and the balance in R is the reason economic sustainability cannot ignore social and environmental impacts.

s: The minimum area of land required to completely sustain the life of the person is called his
x: Ecological footprint is the productive land and sea needed to meet a person's consumption and absorb wastes. Biota, biome and niche are not measures of area required to sustain a person.

s: How is Green GDP obtained?
o: Adding only gross industrial output to conventional GDP
Subtracting unpaid household work from GDP
Adjusting GDP for natural-resource depletion and environmental damage
Measuring only the value of protected forests
x: Green GDP adjusts conventional GDP to account for natural-resource depletion and environmental damage.

s: Which measure of sustainability adds unpaid work and subtracts pollution, crime and resource loss?
x: The Genuine Progress Indicator makes these adjustments; Earth Overshoot Day marks when humanity's demand exceeds what Earth can regenerate that year.

s: What does the ecological footprint of a population refer to?
o: Annual date on which its natural resources are exhausted
Amount of carbon dioxide emitted by its industries alone
Productive land and sea needed to meet its consumption and absorb its wastes
Total number of endangered species in its territory
x: An ecological footprint estimates the productive land and sea area required to supply consumption and absorb generated wastes, expressed in global hectares.

s: Who conceived Earth Overshoot Day?
x: Earth Overshoot Day was conceived by Andrew Simms of the New Economics Foundation, UK; the first campaign was in 2006.

s: In which unit is the ecological footprint measured?
x: The ecological footprint is the productive land and sea needed to meet consumption and absorb wastes, measured in global hectares.

s: With which organisation did the first Earth Overshoot Day campaign of 2006 begin?
x: Earth Overshoot Day was conceived by Andrew Simms; its first campaign in 2006 was with the Global Footprint Network.
